key_facts: Thales Australia built the armed Guardian Angel UGV from concept to live-fire testing in six weeks, working with Chaos 1 and W&E Platt.
The Guardian Angel is a prototype not built specifically for market, part of a program to strengthen autonomous systems capability.
The Guardian Angel features W&E Platt's Remote Operated Weapon PLATTform mounting a Dillon M134D Minigun.

The Australian Army is separately trialing multiple other UGVs including BAE Systems Australia's M113AS4 conversions and ATLAS 8x8, Cyborg Dynamics Engineering's Warfighter UGV, Outlook Industries' GUS, GaardTech's Jaegar-C, and DefendTex's Banshee.
Brigadier Ben McLennan of the Australian Army's 3rd Brigade said UGVs will be used in upcoming exercises for tasks like minefield breaching.
